event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: The 10-K excerpts show that CTAS treats the COVID-19 pandemic as both an already-realized shock and a continuing source of uncertainty.  The company cites concrete, historical consequences (loss of normal operations, slower customer payments, extra inventory and reserves taken, adverse impacts on consolidated results) while simultaneously warning that future outcomes remain unknowable and highly dependent on external factors outside management’s control (government mandates, pace of economic recovery, supplier stability, etc.).  Disclosures cover multiple vectors—demand contraction, supply-chain and labor flow restrictions, working-capital pressure, and the need for operational pivots such as PPE inventory builds.  Language is largely qualitative (no dollar figures) but clearly connects the pandemic to material impacts on sales, costs and cash flows, indicating an elevated but not catastrophic risk.  Because the filing date (July 2022) is only ~2 years after the WHO declaration (March 2020), the Time Decay Principle permits high severity scores (upper-mid to high single digits).  Statements that describe direct, realized impacts earn higher scores; broad, generic or partially mitigated statements are tempered downward, while sentences that highlight favourable offsets (vaccine roll-out, restriction easing) receive deductions.  Overall, CTAS’s pandemic risk profile is assessed as significant and ongoing, though gradually moderating as mitigation efforts take effect.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has created widespread disruption in the global economy and has had, and could continue to have, an adverse impact on our consolidated results of operations and financial performance, as well as on the results of operations and financial performance of many of the customers and suppliers in industries that we serve and operate.

components.reason: States pandemic already HAD an adverse impact on CTAS results (realised impact).
Adds forward-looking clause 'could continue to have' (ongoing risk).
Extends impact to customers and suppliers, signalling ecosystem vulnerability.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Directly links COVID-19 to realised and continuing adverse effects on CTAS and its value chain; high but unquantified impact warrants a 7.

evidence_list.snippet: Since fiscal 2020, the existence of the COVID-19 pandemic, the fear associated with the COVID-19 pandemic and the reactions of governments around the world in response to the COVID-19 pandemic to regulate the flow of labor and products and impede the business of our customers, impacted our ability to conduct normal business operations, which had an adverse effect on our business.

components.reason: Specifies time-anchored, realised impact ('impacted our ability to conduct normal business operations').
Details mechanisms (labor and product flow restrictions) showing supply-chain and workforce strain.
Concludes with 'adverse effect on our business' signalling materiality.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Gives concrete operational disruption already experienced; strong but still qualitative, so scored 6.

evidence_list.snippet: Many of Cintas' customers were also impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic, and we saw an impact on some customer's ability to pay timely.
